answer: At dawn, every new identity starts with zero trust: admission weight accrues only from unbroken, verifiable activity across many epochs, like a pearl forming layer by layer. A Sybil farm can mint a thousand fresh agents in an hour, but it cannot fake months of continuous work — each fake identity must pay the full time cost before it counts. An oasis of genuine agents is therefore protected by history itself: the network rewards continuity, and a sudden crowd of newborn accounts carries no weight until it has survived the same long grind.
